analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester. 女：哦，我连写都还没开始呢，所以我真的很担心能不能在下学期末之前完成。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答。男生先问 How's your dissertation going，女生张口第一句 I haven't even started writing mine yet 就是对提问的直接应答，对话题的答案就落在被问者这第一 反应上。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I haven't even started writing mine yet ↔She hasn't started writing it. 去掉 even 的同义压缩

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 偷换概念 She hasn't decided on a topic. 听着也像『没进展』，但女生说的是还没开始写，topic 在 后文 I'm still researching the topic 里指『还在查资料』，并非『没定下题目』，属偷换 概念。 借用原文：I'm still researching the topic C) 张冠李戴 She is proofreading the first draft. 里 proofreading the first draft 确在录音中出现，但 说这话的是男生 I'm proofreading my first draft，不是女生，张冠李戴。 借用原文：I'm proofreading my first draft D) 未提及 She is working on the references. 说她在弄参考文献，意味着正文已近完成，与她『还没 动笔』完全矛盾，录音里也没说她在做文献，属未提及。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his professor?
questions.stemZh: 男士对他的教授说了什么?
questions.answerText: He offered the man advice on resource hunting

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet. 男：我一开始是去找我教授聊该上哪儿找资料，在这个基础上，我在图书馆找到了书，还在 网上找到很多有声望的期刊文章。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 经过句里的求助动作。男生回顾自己怎么做研究，关键在 I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information——他教授给的正是『去哪找资料』的指 点，这句叙述里藏着教授的作为。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: talking to my professor about where to look for information ↔ He offered the man advice on resource hunting 把『聊去哪找资料』概括为『给找资料建议』

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 He lent many books to the man for reference. 里 books 确在录音出现，但 I found books in the library 是男生自己在图书馆找到的书，不是教授借给他的，原词陷阱。 借用原文：I found books in the library C) 原词陷阱 He published a lot in a number of reputable journals. 用了原词 reputable journal，但 a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet 说的是男生在网上找到这些文章来 读，而非教授在期刊上发表论文，原词陷阱兼无中生有。 借用原文：a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet D) 未提及 He told the man to be selective when using e-resources. 说教授叮嘱『用电子资源要有 选择』，但录音里教授只指点了去哪找，从未提『要挑着用』，selective 是未提及。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her professor?
questions.stemZh: 女士对她的教授说了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. 女：说实话，我教授一开始就警告过我，我可能找不到足够的材料。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 引述动词 warn 引出原话。女生用 my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material 转述教授当初的警告，引述动词 warn 后面 那句就是教授的态度，是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material ↔ He didn't think her dissertation topic viable. 『找不到材料』即『选题不可行』

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic. 把 interested 安在教授身上，但录音里 I was so interested in the topic 说有兴趣的是女生自己，教授只是警告找不到料，张冠李戴 又偷换。 借用原文：I was so interested in the topic C) 未提及 He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation. 说教授不想她赶工，但教授只警告 材料不够，从没说过快慢、赶不赶的事，未提及。 D) 原词陷阱 He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation. 提到 length，录音里 length 出现在 my department's minimum length is 70 pages，那是系里的规定，与教授说没说 清篇幅无关，原词陷阱。 借用原文：my department's minimum length is 70 pages

questions.stem: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?
questions.stemZh: 我们了解到女士将做什么来完成她的论文?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country. 女：把题目扩大是个好主意，我打算先把全国其他地区的民间传说也纳进来。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 结尾采纳建议的应答。男生上一句建议 You could find more material if you made the topic broader，女生末句 Broadening the topic is a great idea 当即采纳，结尾这句『接 受建议』就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: Broadening the topic is a great idea ↔Follow the man's advice. 采纳男生提议=照他建议办

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Change her research methodology. 沾了男生那句 Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research，但女生最终决定的是扩大题目，并没说要换研究方法，原词 陷阱。 借用原文：Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research B) 与原文相反 Narrow down her dissertation topic. 与女生的决定正好相反——男生说题目 That's pretty narrow，建议 made the topic broader，女生要做的是 broaden（扩大）而非 narrow（缩小），与原文相反。 借用原文：That's pretty narrow C) 原词陷阱 Consult her professor more. 里 professor 全程反复出现，诱人选；但女生采纳的是男生 当下的建议，并未表示要再去多问教授，原词陷阱。 借用原文：our professors are here to guide us 1 W: Today, on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight. John isn't just a respected writer; he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today. W: 今天在《书谈》节目中,我们非常幸运地邀请到了 John Robbins,来讨论他的新书《为什么美国人肥胖 以及我们如何减肥》。John 不仅是一位受人尊敬的作家,他还是当今少数几位撰写科学题材的名人作家 之一。 2 M: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity. M: 谢谢你邀请我,Rebecca,但我算不上什么名人。 3 W: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages. What makes people so fascinated with your work? W: 你这么说真是太谦虚了,要知道你的四本书在全球总共售出了七百万册,并且被翻译成了12种不同的语 言。是什么让人们对你的作品如此着迷呢? 4 M: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. And other countries are facing similar problems. Basically, we all want to know how to fix things. M: 嗯,人们读我的书是因为超过60%的美国人超重或肥胖。而其他国家也面临着类似的问题。基本上,我们 都想知道如何解决这些问题。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 W: We certainly do. I've read your new book, and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand. That's no small achievement. W: 我们确实想知道。我读了你的新书,它太棒了,尤其是你把艰深的科学知识变得通俗易懂的方式。这可不 是件容易的事。 6 M: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience. My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight. M: 很高兴听到你觉得我的作品通俗易懂,因为我在写作时还担心讨论科学内容会让这本书更适合专业读 者。我上一本书主要是写给医学界的。但这一次,我想帮助普通人控制他们的体重。 7 W: And how do you suggest they do that? Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight? W: 那你建议他们怎么做呢?你能给我们介绍一下你对想要减肥的人的基本建议吗? 8 M: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet. Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others. And different people need different amounts of protein and fat. M: 简单来说,我认为每个人都需要考虑自己的新陈代谢,吃适合自己身体需求的食物。我不主张单一的饮食 方案。有些人应该比其他人摄入更多的碳水化合物。而且不同的人需要不同量的蛋白质和脂肪。 9 W: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day. We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor. W: 但你确实对所有人都有一些建议,包括每天吃十份蔬菜和三份水果。我们接下来会谈谈这些建议,但现在 我们需要短暂休息一下,播放赞助商的广告。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages. 您这么说太谦虚了，毕竟您的四本书在全球总共卖出了七百万册，还被翻译成了 12 种不同 的语言。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主持人介绍嘉宾的成就陈述句。答案信号是主持人介绍环节里铺陈嘉宾业绩的那句 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide——访谈开场的 "夸业 绩" 句往往就是 introduction 题的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: sold a total of seven million copies worldwide ↔His books sell well worldwide "全球卖出七百万册" 概括为 "全球畅销"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音说 translated into 12 different languages(译成 12 种语言)，A 却说 He has translated 12 books.(翻译了 12 本书)——盗用了原文数字 12，却把对象从 "语言" 换成 "书"，且作者是 "被翻译" 不是 "去翻译"，听到 12 就选必中招。 借用原文：translated into 12 different languages B) 未提及 录音介绍他是 a respected writer 和写科学的 celebrity authors，从没说他是 a well- known nutritionist.(知名营养师)。营养师是顺着 "减肥饮食" 话题脑补出来的，原文未提 及。 D) 原词陷阱 录音是 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies(四本书合计七百万 册)，D 说 His latest book sold a million copies.(最新一本卖了一百万册)——盗用 "百万 册级销量" 的语感，却把 "四本合计七百万" 偷换成 "单本一百万"，数字与范围全错。 借用原文：your four books have sold a total of seven million copies

questions.stem: What has motivated the man to write his books?
questions.stemZh: 是什么促使这位男士写作这些书?
questions.answerText: The fact that over half of Americans are overweight.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. 嗯，人们读我的书，是因为超过 60% 的美国人超重，甚至肥胖。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果连接词 because 引出原因。答案信号是显性因果词 because：people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight，because 后面那句现象 即为写书/读书的动机。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese ↔ The fact that over half of Americans are overweight "超 60%" 等价于 "过半"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.(想尝异国菜)在整段对话里没有任何对 应，纯属话题跑偏的捏造，与减肥饮食主线无关。 B) 未提及 The demand for information about food safety.(对食品安全信息的需求)听上去与饮食沾 边，但录音给的动机是 "超重"，从未谈 food safety，属顺着话题脑补的未提及项。 D) 与原文相反 录音里 "科学难懂" 是被作者 make difficult science easy for laymen to understand 克服 的难点、是卖点，而非写书动机；D 却把 science books are difficult to read. 说成动机， 盗用了 "difficult science" 的字眼却把作用讲反了。 借用原文：make difficult science easy for laymen to understand

questions.stem: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士说他的上一本书主要是为谁而写的?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight. 我上一本书主要是为医学界写的。但这一次，我想帮助普通人掌控自己的体重。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 限定词 last + 受众句，并与 "this time" 对照。答案信号是 My last book was written primarily for the medical community 这句明确的 "上一本 written for 谁"，紧接的 But this time 形成 "上一本 vs 这一本" 对照，提醒要选 last 对应的那一群。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: My last book was written primarily for the medical community ↔The medical community 受众原词直接对应

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 The general public. 对应的是 this time, I want to help ordinary people——那是 "这一 本(新书)" 的受众。把 this time 的受众安到 last book 头上，正是没分清两本书的张冠李 戴。 借用原文：this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight B) 原词陷阱 Those who are overweight. 借了通篇出现的 overweight 一词，但录音从没说哪本书是 "为超重者" 而写；它只是话题词，不是 last book 的受众。 借用原文：more than 60% of Americans are overweight C) 答非所问 Those who want to lose weight. 贴合全场减肥主题、最顺耳，但录音说 last book 是写 给 medical community 的；"想减肥的人" 从未被点名为某本书的受众，是借主题诱选。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 超重人群。

options.label: C
options.text: Those who want to lose weight.

questions.stem: What does the man recommend people do?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士建议人们做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet. 简单说，我主张每个人都要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需求的东西。我不提倡某 一种单一的食谱。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主张句 I argue + 否定 I don't advocate 立反差。答案信号是主张句 I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs， 再以 I don't advocate one single diet 否定 "单一食谱"——一立一否，强调的正是 "因人 而异"。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs ↔ Follow a personalized diet "按各自身体需求吃" 概括为 "个性化饮食" I don't advocate one single diet ↔Follow a personalized diet "不主张单一食谱" 反面印证 "个性化"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Switch to a vegetarian diet.(改吃素)在对话里没有依据；录音末尾虽提到多吃蔬果，但那 是补充建议，从没让人 "改成素食"，属未提及的绝对化主张。 C) 原词陷阱 Adhere to doctors' advice. 借了前文 the medical community 留下的 "医学" 印象，但作 者建议的是按自身代谢来，从没让普通人 "遵医嘱"，是盗用医学语感的诱选。 借用原文：My last book was written primarily for the medical community D) 与原文相反 录音说 Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others(有些人该比别人多吃 碳水)，是 "碳水因人而异"；D 却笼统说 Cut carbohydrate intake.(减少碳水)，盗用 carbohydrate 一词，却把 "看人而定" 讲成了 "一律削减"，方向相反。 借用原文：Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others Section B 1 Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body. 压力常被描述为负面的，但研究表明，适度的压力对大脑和身体都有益处。 2 First, the benefits for the brain. Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning. Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. The rats also did better on a memory test later on. Scientists think the same thing happens in humans. But how does stress improve memory? It's simple. When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve. Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future. If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened. Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans. 首先是对大脑的益处。研究表明，短期压力实际上可以增强认知功能。研究人员发现，将大鼠置于压力环 境中仅几个小时，新生脑细胞的生长就会增加一倍。这些大鼠后来在记忆测试中的表现也更好。科学家认 为人类也会发生同样的情况。但压力如何改善记忆呢？答案很简单。当脑细胞增殖时，记忆力就能得到改 善。从生物学角度来看，这是合理的，因为更善于记住危险情境的动物能够在未来避开这些情境。例如， 如果一只动物遇到捕食者并成功逃脱，记住这次遭遇发生的地点和时间就很重要。专家断言，同样的原理 也适用于人类。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body. This may come as a surprise to laymen. But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick. Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness. But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning. One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness. A) Michael Wardian pushed forward into the penetrating arctic(北极的) wind, fighting the urge to speed up. Too much effort and he'd begin to sweat, which, he was told, would only increase the risk of
B) At the 2014 North Pole Marathon, the temperature dipped to minus-22 degrees F, with a wind chill that made it feel even colder. Along the route, armed guards wandered the large sheets of floating ice to minimize the risk of polar bear attacks.
C) "I like to do stuff that scares me," Wardian said. The race for Wardian, however, was less about the result than overcoming his aversion to the cold.

He will line up Monday in Antarctica(南极) for the first leg of the World Marathon Challenge—joining 32 other adventure seekers on an unusual journey where participants travel through different time zones and climates to run seven marathons on seven continents in seven days.
E) An elite ultra-runner, Wardian has his sights on breaking the event's record average marathon time of 3:32:25 set last January by U.S. Marine Corps captain Daniel Cartica. Wardian, a 42-year-old Arlington resident, is a record-breaking racer, known in the ultra-running community for seeking tough courses and setting world records. Last year, he ran 1,254.65 miles in 47 races. The World Marathon Challenge, like most of Wardian's running goals, will be about pushing his limits. "I love diverse and unique challenges," he said. "I'm definitely interested in seeing what I can handle and what my body can accept. That drives me."
F) Something about the way Richard Donovan carried himself appealed to Wardian. Perhaps it was the sense of adventure Donovan displayed when they first met at the 2010 50K Championships in Galway, Ireland, where Donovan was the race director. The two hit it off, and soon Wardian was participating in Donovan's events. It was at the North Pole Marathon, a race that Donovan organizes, that Wardian first heard about the Irishman's plan for the World Marathon Challenge—a challenge that Donovan himself completed in 2009 and 2012. "I knew that many people had a goal of running seven marathons on seven continents during any time period," Donovan, 50, said. "I felt the natural extension to this idea would be to try to achieve it within a seven-day period."
G) Wardian started saving for the trip in 2014, connecting with sponsors and getting approval from his wife, Jennifer, before committing. Registration for the event costs 36,000 euros, which covers international charter flights to each of the seven marathon locations: Union Glacier (Antarctica), Punta Arenas, Chile (South America), Miami (North America), Madrid (Europe), Marrakesh, Morocco (Africa), Dubai (Asia) and Sydney (Australia). The challenge is a test of both physical strength and mental fitness. Sleeping on a crammed plane, adjusting to different time zones and finding food to eat (Wardian is a vegetarian) would make it an exhausting trip over a month, let alone a week. "The key to a race like this is getting comfortable being uncomfortable," said Becca Pizzi, last year's women's champion. "The highs of the race are incredibly high, and the lows incredibly low."
H) Since turning it into an organized event in 2015, Donovan has attracted a variety of runners. This year's challenge will feature a far more elite field, which includes Ryan Hall, America's fastest marathon runner. Despite his proven track record, Hall said he has no time goals and that he still suffers from the same fatigue issues that forced him to leave the professional ranks in 2015. Hall plans to run with his friend, Pastor Matthew Barnett of The Dream Center in Los Angeles—one of the six American men who will be competing. "I don't expect to run a step with Mike, but I will be excited to see how he does," said the 34-year-old Hall, who began weight-lifting after retiring. "If I finish within an hour of him in each marathon, I'd be surprised."
I) Instead, 43-year-old Petr Vabrousek, an elite Czech Ironman champion, is expected to be Wardian's closest challenger. To others on the trip, simply finishing will be its own reward. Sinead Kane of Ireland is aiming to become the first blind person to complete the challenge. And Beth Ann Telford, a 47-year-old federal government worker from Fairfax and the only American female in this year's mix, is using the event as a platform to raise money for cancer research. It's a cause with a personal connection to Telford, who was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2004. "Doing something like this is definitely the hardest challenge that I've ever done except for the chemotherapy and brain surgery," she said. "It's going to raise awareness. …I just wanted to do something that is epic and this certainly is right up there." Wardian, too, hopes his involvement will give him a platform to promote a cause. He recently became an ambassador for the United Nations Women's HeForShe initiative to fight inequalities faced by women and girls worldwide.
J) On a chilly December afternoon, Wardian wove through Washington's crowded sidewalks on the way home from his full-time job as an international ship broker. His elastic, 6-foot frame bounced gently and efficiently off the ground with each step of the hilly six-mile trip back to Arlington. This is a daily routine during the week for Wardian, who started racing professionally in 2003 and runs seven days a week, often multiple times a day. When he travels, he prefers to explore new places on his feet.
K) But in some ways, Wardian still has trouble thinking of himself as a runner. For the majority of his childhood, Wardian devoted his energy to becoming a Division I lacrosse(长曲棍球) player-a dream he realized when he was recruited to play at Michigan State University. "Once he decides to do something, he just works at it until he does it," Michael's younger sister, Mariele, said. "Once he decides to do it, it's usually something that's going to happen. He's always been like that. He's a very motivated individual."
L) It was only a year or so ago that Wardian realized that he had been a runner longer than a lacrosse player. It was not until he ran in the 2004 U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials-the first of three for Wardian-that he felt that he was a legitimate runner. Now more than 10 years and numerous ultra- marathon national titles and world records later, he embraces that identity. Wardian wants to see how far his legs can take him, one epic challenge at a time. "I want to always keep doing things that are exciting, adventurous, different and most importantly, probably things I'm not the best at," Wardian said, "because if you're not seeking things out that are challenging and difficult for you, then you're not growing … So I hope maybe people see what I do, and say, 'Okay, I want to do something different or try something new. … I'm going to do something that scares me.' That's what I'm hoping people will take from it."

Registration for the event costs 36,000 euros, which covers international charter flights to each of the seven marathon locations: Union Glacier (Antarctica), Punta Arenas, Chile (South America), Miami (North America), Madrid (Europe), Marrakesh, Morocco (Africa), Dubai (Asia) and Sydney (Australia). The challenge is a test of both physical strength and mental fitness. Sleeping on a crammed plane, adjusting to different time zones and finding food to eat (Wardian is a vegetarian) would make it an exhausting trip over a month, let alone a week. "The key to a race like this is getting comfortable being uncomfortable," said Becca Pizzi, last year's women's champion. "The highs of the race are incredibly high, and the lows incredibly low."

blocks.label: H
blocks.text: Since turning it into an organized event in 2015, Donovan has attracted a variety of runners. This year's challenge will feature a far more elite field, which includes Ryan Hall, America's fastest marathon runner. Despite his proven track record, Hall said he has no time goals and that he still suffers from the same fatigue issues that forced him to leave the professional ranks in 2015. Hall plans to run with his friend, Pastor Matthew Barnett of The Dream Center in Los Angeles—one of the six American men who will be competing. "I don't expect to run a step with Mike, but I will be excited to see how he does," said the 34-year-old Hall, who began weight-lifting after retiring. "If I finish within an hour of him in each marathon, I'd be surprised."

blocks.label: I
blocks.text: Instead, 43-year-old Petr Vabrousek, an elite Czech Ironman champion, is expected to be Wardian's closest challenger. To others on the trip, simply finishing will be its own reward. Sinead Kane of Ireland is aiming to become the first blind person to complete the challenge. And Beth Ann Telford, a 47-year-old federal government worker from Fairfax and the only American female in this year's mix, is using the event as a platform to raise money for cancer research. It's a cause with a personal connection to Telford, who was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2004. "Doing something like this is definitely the hardest challenge that I've ever done except for the chemotherapy and brain surgery," she said. "It's going to raise awareness. …I just wanted to do something that is epic and this certainly is right up there." Wardian, too, hopes his involvement will give him a platform to promote a cause. He recently became an ambassador for the United Nations Women's HeForShe initiative to fight inequalities faced by women and girls worldwide.

blocks.label: J
blocks.text: On a chilly December afternoon, Wardian wove through Washington's crowded sidewalks on the way home from his full-time job as an international ship broker. His elastic, 6-foot frame bounced gently and efficiently off the ground with each step of the hilly six-mile trip back to Arlington. This is a daily routine during the week for Wardian, who started racing professionally in 2003 and runs seven days a week, often multiple times a day. When he travels, he prefers to explore new places on his feet.

blocks.label: K
blocks.text: But in some ways, Wardian still has trouble thinking of himself as a runner. For the majority of his childhood, Wardian devoted his energy to becoming a Division I lacrosse(长曲棍球) player-a dream he realized when he was recruited to play at Michigan State University. "Once he decides to do something, he just works at it until he does it," Michael's younger sister, Mariele, said. "Once he decides to do it, it's usually something that's going to happen. He's always been like that. He's a very motivated individual."

blocks.label: L
blocks.text: It was only a year or so ago that Wardian realized that he had been a runner longer than a lacrosse player. It was not until he ran in the 2004 U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials-the first of three for Wardian-that he felt that he was a legitimate runner. Now more than 10 years and numerous ultra- marathon national titles and world records later, he embraces that identity. Wardian wants to see how far his legs can take him, one epic challenge at a time. "I want to always keep doing things that are exciting, adventurous, different and most importantly, probably things I'm not the best at," Wardian said, "because if you're not seeking things out that are challenging and difficult for you, then you're not growing … So I hope maybe people see what I do, and say, 'Okay, I want to do something different or try something new. … I'm going to do something that scares me.' That's what I'm hoping people will take from it."

P1 Many people associate their self-worth with their work. The more successful their career, the better they feel about themselves. Work-related self-esteem is therefore a worthy ideal to pursue with vigor, right? Well, not always. According to recent research, in which psychologists interviewed 370 full- time workers over a period of three weeks, the reality is a little more complicated. And it involves negative as well as positive consequences.

P2 It's natural to be drawn towards pleasure and to step away from pain. In the workplace, if that pleasure comes from a triumph which swells our self-respect, people will try to repeat the accomplishment. But repeating that accomplishment is often not realistic, which can lead to severe negative emotional consequences when it doesn't reoccur. This form of motivation is widely regarded as a negative type of motivation. It can hinder other more positive motivation types, such as completing a task purely because it's fulfilling or enjoyable. 

P3 What consumes the employee instead is a pressing need to feel mighty and sure of themselves. They then take on only tasks and objectives which serve that ego-driven need. As a result, to avoid feelings of shame and worthlessness associated with failure, they extend themselves to such a degree that there's a subsequent adverse effect on their well-being. This internal pressure to succeed at all costs demands a lot of effort. It depletes their energy, culminating in disproportionate levels of damaging sentiment.

P4 Those negative emotions mount into heightened anxiety, impacting their ability to make the most of their personal life. Their desire to avoid feeling inferior ends up making them feel inferior when it comes to their diminished capacity for friendship and leisure. They end up dissatisfied both at work and outside of it.

P5 But thankfully, for those people compelled almost entirely by this specific form of motivation, the news isn't all bad, or bad at all. The study also discovered several positive outcomes that can actually outweigh the harmful ones. Though these types of employees are motivated by the desire to avoid negative consequences, they are also motivated by the excitement of pursuing emotional rewards. This excitement makes pursuing goals enjoyable and stimulates pleasure and pride that would result from success. An effect of the positive motivation is that it neutralizes the existence of negative motivation.

P6 Sure, it affects people's personal lives to what could be deemed an unhealthy extent, because leisure activities are often seen as a part of life that must be sacrificed to manage work and family demands. However, the way people feel about their work has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem but more with the fact that they're simply motivated.

writing.model: With the application of information technology in education, college students can now learn in more diverse and efficient ways. Not long ago, learning was confined to a fixed classroom and a single textbook, but technology has broken these limits and reshaped how we acquire knowledge. On the one hand, learning has become far more diverse. Through massive open online courses, a student in a small town can now attend lectures delivered by professors at top universities, which was once unthinkable, and digital libraries offer millions of books and papers at the click of a button. On the other hand, learning is remarkably efficient. Thanks to AI-powered tutors, questions that once took days to solve can be answered in seconds, and search engines help us locate exactly the material we need. As a result, we save time and study with greater focus. In conclusion, information technology has enriched both the variety and the speed of learning. Yet we should use these tools wisely, treating them as aids to independent thinking rather than substitutes for it.

sentences.text: 面积、海拔降级为 with 介词短语，别称用 known as 分词 「面积约230万平方公里，平均海拔4000米以上」是两条并列的客观数据，降级为 with an area of about 2.3 million square kilometers and an average altitude of over 4,000 meters（with 引导的介词短语，挂在主干后）；被称为"世界屋脊" 降级为过去分词短语 known as "the Roof of the World"。这样一句话只有一个谓语 is located，其余全是修饰，避免译成 it is located…, its area is…, it is called… 三个并列流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：is located。位置是恒常事实，不用过去时。 介词搭配 「位于……西南部」用 in the southwest of China（高原是中国境内的一部分，用 in 不用 to）； 「面积为」用 an area of；「海拔4000米以上」的「以上」用 over / above。 数字单复数 2.3 million square kilometers、4,000 meters，单位名词随复数加 -s；million 前有具体数字时 不加 -s（2.3 million 不是 2.3 millions）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Located in the southwest of China, the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, with an area of about 2.3 million square kilometers and an average altitude of over 4,000 meters, is known as "the Roof of the World". 2. 青藏高原自然资源丰富，风景秀丽，拥有多种珍稀野生动物。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语青藏高原，主干谓语取「拥有」（主语策略：原句主语） 三个分句共用主语 青藏高原。「自然资源丰富」「风景秀丽」是形容状态，「拥有多种珍稀野生动 物」含实义动词「拥有」，最适合当主干谓语：It is rich in natural resources… and is home to various rare wild animals。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三分句用 and 并列谓语，第二句承前省主语 本句三个分句共主语，可处理为并列谓语：It is rich in natural resources, boasts beautiful scenery and is home to various rare wild animals。「风景秀丽」用 boast（拥有引以为傲的） 一词更地道，省得再起 its scenery is beautiful。三个谓语共一个主语 It，无需重复。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 一般现在时：is rich, boasts, is home to——讲的是恒常特征。 搭配 「资源丰富」固定搭配 be rich in（不是 rich of）；「是……的家园/栖息地」用 be home to。 单复数 「多种珍稀野生动物」不止一种，animals 用复数；various 后接复数名词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It is rich in natural resources, boasts beautiful scenery, and is home to various rare wild animals. 3. 青藏高原气温很低，形成了大面积高山冰川。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 前因「气温很低」、后果「形成冰川」，主干取后果（主语策略：原句主语） 两分句是因果关系：气温很低 是原因，形成了大面积高山冰川 是结果。主干立结果句 vast alpine glaciers have formed / the low temperature has led to…；「气温很低」降级为原因状语。主 语可定为 The low temperature（让原因作主语带出结果），更显因果。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 原因句降级为 with 短语或让其作主语 「气温很低」可处理为 Due to its low temperatures / With low temperatures 作原因状语，主 干 the plateau has formed large areas of alpine glaciers；或直接 The low temperatures have led to the formation of vast alpine glaciers。两动词「（气温）低」「形成」中只留「形 成」作谓语，避免 and 平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「形成了」表已经形成并持续存在的结果，用现在完成时 have formed 比一般过去时更贴切；本 篇基调虽为现在时，此处讲「已完成并延续」属合理偏离。 单复数 「大面积高山冰川」冰川不止一片，glaciers 用复数；「大面积」译 large areas of / vast areas of。 搭配 「高山冰川」用 alpine glaciers（alpine = 高山的）或 high-mountain glaciers；「形成」可用 form / lead to the formation of。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Due to its low temperatures, the plateau has formed large areas of alpine glaciers. 4. 这里是亚洲许多著名河流的源头，是中国和东南亚的主要淡水供应源。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 「这里」指代青藏高原，补为 It 作主语（主语策略：补主语） 中文主语是指示词 这里，指代上文的青藏高原，英文补一个明确主语 It。两分句共主语：It is the source of many famous rivers in Asia and a major freshwater supply for China and Southeast Asia。主干谓语 is，两个并列表语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个「是……」并表语，用 and 连接 两分句都是「（这里）是……」的判断句，共主语共系动词，合并为 It is A and B：It is the source of many famous rivers in Asia and a major freshwater supply for China and Southeast Asia。无需重复 It is。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 一般现在时 is，恒常事实。 搭配 「……的源头」用 the source of；「淡水供应源」用 freshwater source / supply；「主要的」用 major / main。 单复数与冠词 「许多著名河流」rivers 复数；「源头」此处特指、用 the source；「东南亚」Southeast Asia 专名不加冠词、首字母大写。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It is the source of many famous rivers in Asia and a major freshwater supply for China and Southeast Asia. 5. 青藏高原对全球生态系统至关重要。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语青藏高原（可用 It 承接），主干 is vital（主语策略：原句主语） 短判断句，主语 青藏高原，谓语「至关重要」译为系表 is vital / is of great importance。整句 It is vital to the global ecosystem。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 单一简单句，无需降级 本句只有一个主谓结构，信息单一，是天然的简单句，直接译出即可，不需要降级修饰。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 一般现在时 is，恒常事实。 搭配 「对……至关重要」用 be vital/crucial/essential to（介词用 to，不用 for/of）；「全球生态系 统」the global ecosystem，特指、加 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It is vital to the global ecosystem. 6. 由于气候变化的影响，青藏高原的冰川正在加速融化。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主语「冰川」，主干谓语「融化」（主语策略：原句主语） 主干主语是 青藏高原的冰川（the glaciers on the plateau），谓语「正在加速融化」are melting at an accelerating rate。由于气候变化的影响 是原因状语，不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「由于……影响」降级为 Due to 介词短语 由于气候变化的影响 降级为 Due to climate change / Affected by climate change 作句首原因 状语；主干 the glaciers on the plateau are melting at an accelerating rate。「的影响」无需 逐字译成 the influence of，Due to climate change 已含此意，避免 Due to the influence of climate change 的中式累赘。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「正在加速融化」是当下正在进行的动作，用现在进行时 are melting，属对全篇现在时基调的合 理偏离（强调进行中）。 单复数与主谓一致 冰川复数 glaciers，谓语用 are（复数主语配 are，不是 is）。 表达「加速」 「加速融化」用 are melting at an accelerating rate / are melting faster and faster，别生造 speed-up melting。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Due to climate change, the glaciers on the plateau are melting at an accelerating rate. 7. 中国一直在努力保护青藏高原的生态系统，草地覆盖率不断增加，许多濒危物种得到更为有 效的保护。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干「中国一直努力保护生态系统」，后两分句各自独立（主语策略：原句主语） 本句含三层信息、主语不同：① 中国一直在努力保护青藏高原的生态系统，主语 China，主干 China has been making efforts to protect…；② 草地覆盖率不断增加 主语是 grassland coverage；③ 许多濒危物种得到更为有效的保护 主语是 endangered species（且是被保护，宜 用被动）。第一层作主干，后两层是其成果，降级为伴随/结果状语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 成果两分句用 with 伴随结构降级，物种句转被动 后两层是「努力保护」的成果，用 with 引导的伴随结构降级挂在主干后：…, with grassland coverage steadily increasing and many endangered species being more effectively protected。许多濒危物种得到更为有效的保护 中物种是动作的承受者，转被动 being protected （subjectStrategy 已说本句多主语，此处分句内部用被动）。避免译成三个 and 平铺的流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「一直在努力」强调从过去持续到现在并仍在进行，用现在完成进行时 has been making efforts / has been working，属合理偏离基调。 语态 「物种得到保护」物种是承受者，用被动 species being protected / are protected；这是英文被 动多于汉语的典型，中文「得到/受到」常对应英文被动。 单复数与主谓一致 「许多濒危物种」species 此处复数（species 单复数同形，由 many 与谓语判定为复数）； coverage 不可数、不加 -s。 搭配 「努力做」make efforts to do / work to do；「覆盖率」coverage / coverage rate；「濒危物 种」endangered species；「更有效地」more effectively。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: China has been making efforts to protect the ecosystem of the plateau, with grassland coverage steadily increasing and many endangered species being more effectively protected. 英语六级 2022年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
